Majutsu is an Emacs interface for the Jujutsu (jj) version control system,
modeled on Magit: a log you can act on, diffs you can select from, and
transients for jj's commands.

* Introduction
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: introduction
:EXPORT_FILE_NAME: guide/introduction
:DESCRIPTION: Understand Majutsu's purpose, Jujutsu model, and project origins.
:END:
** About Majutsu
Majutsu shows a Jujutsu repository in Emacs buffers: the log, diffs, files
as of a revision, bookmarks, operations.  Commands start from what is at
point, and most open a transient in which you pick revisions from the log
before anything runs.  It is built on Magit's sections and on the Transient
package, so it will feel familiar to Magit users.

** About Jujutsu
Jujutsu (jj) is a version control system whose working copy is represented by a
commit. Unlike Git, it has no staging area: the working-copy commit is marked
=@=, and jj snapshots filesystem changes into it at the beginning of most
commands. Mutable history and conflicts are first-class parts of Jujutsu's
model, making rebasing, squashing, and conflict resolution ordinary operations.

** Acknowledgments
- Majutsu began as a fork of =jj-mode.el= by Brandon Olivier.
- Its interface, and much of its code, follows Magit.
- It exists because of Jujutsu and the people who build it.

* Installation
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: installation
:EXPORT_FILE_NAME: guide/installation
:DESCRIPTION: Install Majutsu and verify its Emacs, Jujutsu, and package requirements.
:END:
** Requirements
- Emacs 31.1 or later.
- Jujutsu (jj) 0.47.0 or later, in your =PATH=.
- =magit= 4.4.0 or later (for section management).
- =consult= 1.0 or later and =plz= 0.9.1 or later (for native Gerrit
  completion).
- =transient= 0.13.0 or later (popup menus).
- =with-editor= (for editing descriptions).
- =ghostel= (optional; runs terminal programs such as =jj arrange= and jj's
  built-in diff editor).
- Evil, Embark, Forge, and Org are supported when present; see
  [[#integrations][Integrations]].

** Installing from Git
Majutsu is installed from its GitHub repository.

*** Doom Emacs
Add the following to your =packages.el=:
#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(package! majutsu :recipe (:host github :repo "0WD0/majutsu"))
#+end_src

*** use-package with straight.el
#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(use-package majutsu
  :straight (:host github :repo "0WD0/majutsu"))
#+end_src

*** use-package =:vc= (Emacs 30+)
The built-in =use-package= =:vc= keyword is available in Emacs 30 and later.
Use =:rev :newest= to follow the repository's current default branch:
#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(use-package majutsu
  :vc (:url "https://github.com/0WD0/majutsu"
       :rev :newest))
#+end_src

*** package-vc (Emacs 29+)
Emacs 29 added built-in =package-vc= support. Install Majutsu directly, then
configure it with =use-package=:
#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(unless (package-installed-p 'majutsu)
  (package-vc-install
   '(majutsu :url "https://github.com/0WD0/majutsu")))

(use-package majutsu)
#+end_src

*** Manual Installation
Clone the repository and add it to your =load-path=:
#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(add-to-list 'load-path "/path/to/majutsu")
(require 'majutsu)
#+end_src

** Post-Installation Tasks
#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
*Vanilla:* No keymap setup is required; Majutsu's native bindings are active
as soon as its modes load.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
*Evil:* Majutsu detects Evil, installs its normal-state integration by default,
and opens Majutsu buffers in the configured Evil state.  Customize this with
=M-x customize-group RET majutsu-evil RET=.

* Getting Started
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: getting-started
:EXPORT_FILE_NAME: guide/getting-started
:DESCRIPTION: Open a repository, inspect its history, and learn the essential Majutsu controls.
:END:
Start from a file or Dired buffer whose ~default-directory~ is inside an
existing Jujutsu repository, then run ~M-x majutsu-log~ (the shorter
~M-x majutsu~ is an alias).  With a prefix argument, or when the current
directory is outside a repository, Majutsu asks which directory to use.  If
that directory is not a repository either, it asks before running =jj git
init=; declining leaves the directory unchanged.

The log shows the revision graph.  The working copy is the revision marked
=@=.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
*Vanilla:* Use ~n~ and ~p~ to move by revision section.  ~TAB~ expands or
collapses the section at point, while ~[~ and ~]~ move to a visible parent or
child.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
*Evil:* Majutsu starts the log in Normal state.  Use ~C-j~ and ~C-k~ to move by
section; ~g j~ and ~g k~ move between sibling sections.  ~TAB~ expands or
collapses the section at point, while ~[~ and ~]~ move to a visible parent or
child.

Point is significant: commands opened from the log use the revision under
point as their default.

Press ~RET~ on a revision to see its diff.  Looking never changes anything;
moving the working copy to another revision is the explicit ~e~
(=jj edit=).

#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
*Vanilla:* ~TAB~ folds files or hunks, ~n~ and ~p~ move through sections, and
~q~ returns to the log.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
*Evil:* ~TAB~ folds files or hunks, ~C-j~ and ~C-k~ move through sections, and
~q~ returns to the log without leaving Normal state.

For an explicit selection, press ~d~ in the log to open the Diff transient.
Its =-r/r= entry has two paths: =-r= reads a revset, while ~r~ toggles the
revision at point into the =--revisions= selection.  Press ~d~ to execute the
diff, or ~c~ to clear the selection first.  This does not invoke a rewrite
command, although jj may snapshot changed working-copy files before producing
output.  Selections only become arguments when an action is executed.

Use ~?~ to open the dispatcher and see the commands valid in the current
buffer.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
*Vanilla:* A safe first loop is: move through the log, inspect a diff, return
with ~q~, and refresh with ~g~.  If a jj command fails, press ~$~ to open the
process buffer and read its complete output.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
*Evil:* A safe first loop is: move through the log in Normal state, inspect a
diff, return with ~q~, and refresh with ~g r~.  If a jj command fails, press
~`~ to open the process buffer and read its complete output.

The commands in [[#manipulating][Manipulating]] rewrite history; the
destructive ones ask first, and ~C-/~ (Evil: ~u~) undoes the last operation.

* Interface Concepts
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: interface-concepts
:EXPORT_FILE_NAME: guide/interface-concepts
:DESCRIPTION: Understand Majutsu buffers, sections, transients, selections, and command execution.
:END:
** Buffers
Majutsu buffers are generated from =jj= output and are read-only.  Each
kind has its own major mode, derived from ~majutsu-mode~ and through it
from ~magit-section-mode~.

| Buffer               | Shows                                                    |
|----------------------+----------------------------------------------------------|
| Log                  | The revision graph, working copy status, and workspaces  |
| Diff                 | The changes of a revision, or between two revisions      |
| Blob                 | One file as of one revision                              |
| Bookmark list        | Local bookmarks and the state of their remotes           |
| Remote list          | Git remotes and the bookmarks they hold                  |
| Tag list             | Tags                                                     |
| Workspace list       | The repository's workspaces                              |
| Operation log        | What happened to the repository                          |
| Evolution log        | Earlier versions of one change                           |
| Process              | Recent jj commands and their output                      |

These keys work in all of them:

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: ? (majutsu-dispatch) :: Show the commands available here.
- Key: RET (majutsu-visit-thing) :: Visit the thing at point.
- Key: k (Vanilla) (majutsu-delete-thing) :: Delete the thing at point.
- Key: x (Evil) (majutsu-delete-thing) :: Delete the thing at point.
- Key: g (Vanilla) (majutsu-refresh) :: Refresh the buffer.
- Key: g r (Evil) (majutsu-refresh) :: Refresh the buffer.
- Key: q (majutsu-mode-bury-buffer) :: Bury the buffer.

What visiting and deleting mean depends on the section at point:

| At point                  | Visit                         | Delete             |
|---------------------------+-------------------------------+--------------------|
| Revision in the log       | Show its diff                 | Abandon it         |
| Bookmark                  | Show the diff of its revision | Delete the bookmark |
| Tag                       | Show the diff of its revision | Delete the tag     |
| Remote                    |                               | Remove the remote  |
| Workspace                 | Visit the workspace           |                    |
| File or hunk in a diff    | Visit the file                |                    |
| Evolution log entry       | Show its inter-diff           |                    |
| Command in the process buffer |                           | Kill the process   |
| URL                       | Open it in a browser          |                    |

** Sections
Majutsu organizes information into collapsible sections.  ~TAB~ toggles the
section at point, such as a revision description in the log or a file in a
diff.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
*Vanilla:* ~n~ and ~p~ move forward and backward through sections.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
*Evil:* ~C-j~ and ~C-k~ move forward and backward through sections in Normal,
Visual, and Motion states; ~g j~ and ~g k~ move between siblings.

** Transients
Commands are grouped into transients: popup menus, built with Emacs'
Transient package, in which you set options before running a command.
~r~, for example, opens the Rebase transient.

The main action of a transient has its own key and also runs on ~RET~;
customize ~majutsu-transient-default-action~ to use another key.

*** Saved Defaults
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: saved-defaults
:END:
The Log, Diff, operation log, Fetch, Push, and Gerrit Upload transients can
remember their options.  ~w~ opens the defaults transient:

| Key   | Saves the options for | Cleared by |
|-------+-----------------------+------------|
| ~w u~ | the user              | ~w U~      |
| ~w r~ | this repository       | ~w R~      |
| ~w w~ | this workspace        | ~w W~      |

~s~ sets the options for this workspace until Emacs exits.  The most
specific layer wins: session, workspace, repository, user, built-in.  A
layer replaces the whole option list; layers are not merged.

Saving does not run the command.  One-off values, such as the revisions of
a diff or the bookmarks of a push, are not saved.  In the Log transient, ~0~
resets the options of the current buffer and leaves saved defaults alone.

A log or diff buffer that is already open keeps its own options.
~majutsu-prefix-use-buffer-arguments~ and
~majutsu-direct-use-buffer-arguments~ decide when a transient or a direct
command starts from them.

The defaults are stored in ~transient-values-file~, not in jj's
configuration.  Additional workspaces share the repository layer and have
their own workspace layer.

** Selecting Revisions
Transients that take revisions, such as Rebase, Squash, or Diff, let you pick
them in the log.  An entry shown as =-r/r= has two keys: =-r= reads a revset
in the minibuffer, and ~r~ toggles the revision at point.  Selected
revisions stay highlighted, one color per role, until the command runs or
~c~ clears them.

For example, to rebase a change onto another:
#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
#+attr_demo: :capture rebase-in-log
- ~n n~ :: Move to the change to rebase.
- ~r~ :: Open the Rebase transient.  The log stays live under it.
- ~s~ :: Mark the revision at point as the source.
- ~n n~ :: Move to where it should go.
- ~o~ :: Mark that revision as the destination.
- ~RET~ :: Run the rebase; Majutsu asks first.
- ~y~ :: The change and its descendants now sit on the destination.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
#+attr_demo: :capture rebase-in-log-evil
- ~j j~ :: Move to the change to rebase.
- ~r~ :: Open the Rebase transient.  The log stays live under it.
- ~s~ :: Mark the revision at point as the source.
- ~j j~ :: Move to where it should go.
- ~o~ :: Mark that revision as the destination.
- ~RET~ :: Run the rebase; Majutsu asks first.
- ~y~ :: The change and its descendants now sit on the destination.

With an active region, an argument that can be repeated takes every
revision in the region; an argument that takes one value uses one revision.
Majutsu passes revisions, not expressions: it does not turn a region into
=A..B=.  Type such revsets at the =-r= prompt.

Without a selection, a command uses the revision at point, or the default
its own section of this manual names.

** Filesets
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: filesets
:END:
The =--= entry of a transient limits the command to some files.  It reads jj
fileset expressions, several separated by commas:

#+begin_example
src/main.el, docs
glob:"**/*.org"
src & ~glob:"**/*-test.el"
#+end_example

Completion works on the path being typed, wherever it is in the expression,
and offers the pattern kinds, such as =glob:= and =root:=, where a pattern
can start.  Anything you type is accepted.

Diff, Split, Squash, Absorb, and Restore complete the paths that the transient's
revisions change, since those are the only ones the command can act on.
Log completes any path, one directory level at a time, so a large
repository is never listed whole.

** Completion and Confirmation
Prompts use Emacs' completion, so Vertico, Ivy, and similar interfaces
work.  Revset prompts complete whole expressions with candidates from jj and
label each one with its kind, such as bookmark, tag, or workspace.

Destructive commands such as Abandon, Undo, and Restore ask first; see
[[#customizing][Confirmation Settings]].

** Running jj
Every jj command Majutsu runs is recorded, with its output, in the
repository's process buffer.  Fetch, Push, Gerrit upload, diff editors, and
anything that waits for an editor run in the background; other commands
finish before control returns.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: $ (Vanilla) (majutsu-process-buffer) :: Show the process buffer.
  ~k~ on a running command kills it.
- Key: ` (Evil) (majutsu-process-buffer) :: Show the process buffer.
  ~x~ on a running command kills it.
- Key: ! (majutsu-command) :: Open the Run transient.
- Key: : (Vanilla) (majutsu-jj-command) :: Read a jj command line and run it
  in the current directory.
- Key: | (Evil) (majutsu-jj-command) :: Read a jj command line and run it
  in the current directory.

The Run transient runs any command in the background and shows its output in the
process buffer:

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Run transient"
- Key: ! (majutsu-jj-command-topdir) :: Run a jj command in the workspace root.
- Key: p (majutsu-jj-command) :: Run a jj command in the current directory.
- Key: s (majutsu-shell-command-topdir) :: Run a shell command in the
  workspace root.
- Key: S (majutsu-shell-command) :: Run a shell command in the current
  directory.

~TAB~ completes jj subcommands, options, and their values.

* Inspecting
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: inspecting
:EXPORT_FILE_NAME: workflows/inspecting
:DESCRIPTION: Inspect revisions, diffs, files, and operation history.
:END:
This page covers the log: what a revision row shows, how to move around,
which options filter it, and how to copy from it.  The
[[#files-diffs-operations][Files, Diffs, and Operations]] page continues from
a revision into diffs, files, annotations, Ediff, and jj's operation history.

** Log Buffer
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: log-buffer
:END:
~majutsu-log~ shows the revision graph, followed by the working copy status
and the repository's workspaces.

*** Log Display
Each revision is a section.  Its first line shows the change id, bookmarks,
tags, and the first line of the description, with the commit id, author, and
date aligned to the right.  The rest of a description is the section's body;
~TAB~ folds it.

The graph is jj's.  Lines between revisions, such as =(elided revisions)=,
are decoration: point skips them, and they are neither searched nor copied.

A description too long for the window is cut with … so that the right-hand
columns stay aligned.  Only the display is cut; set
~majutsu-log-elide-description~ to nil to show descriptions in full.

In the jjosh build a revision also lists the projects it touches, such as
=[appkit, chidu]=.  Customize ~majutsu-log-template-touched-projects~ to
change the format.

The columns are configurable; see [[#log-columns][Log Columns]].

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Log buffer" :mode majutsu-log-mode :scope Vanilla
- Key: n (majutsu-goto-next-revision) :: Move to the next revision in display order.
- Key: p (majutsu-goto-prev-revision) :: Move to the previous revision in display order.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Log buffer" :mode majutsu-log-mode
- Key: [ (majutsu-log-goto-parent) :: Jump to a visible parent.  With several
  parents, choose one; candidates show the description.
- Key: ] (majutsu-log-goto-child) :: Jump to a visible child.
- Key: . (Evil) (majutsu-log-goto-@) :: Jump to the working copy.

*** Log Options Transient
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: l (Vanilla) (majutsu-log-transient) :: Open the log options transient.
- Key: L (Evil) (majutsu-log-transient) :: Open the log options transient.

#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Log options transient"
- Key: -r :: Filter by a revset, such as =all()=, =mine()=, or =A | B=.  The
  current filter is offered for editing; empty input clears it.
- Key: -n :: Limit the number of revisions shown.
- Key: -v :: Toggle reverse order.
- Key: -G :: Toggle the graph.
- Key: -- :: Show only revisions that touch the given
  [[#filesets][filesets]].  Completion offers any path, one directory level
  at a time.  Diffs opened from the log are limited to the same filesets.
- Key: g :: Apply the options to the log.
- Key: s :: Apply them and keep them for this workspace until Emacs exits.
- Key: w :: Save them as defaults; see [[#saved-defaults][Saved Defaults]].
- Key: 0 :: Reset the options.

*** Conflicts Section
~majutsu-log-insert-conflicts~ is an optional log section: the working
copy's [[#conflicts-section][Conflicts section]], the one a conflicted
revision has in its diff.

#+begin_src emacs-lisp
(add-hook 'majutsu-log-sections-hook #'majutsu-log-insert-conflicts t)
#+end_src

*** Copying
The log, evolution log, and operation log share a copy transient.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Copy dispatcher"
- Key: ? w s (majutsu-copy-section-value) :: Copy the value of the current
  section, such as a change id.
- Key: ? w f (majutsu-row-copy-field) :: Copy the field at point as displayed.
- Key: ? w F (majutsu-row-copy-entry-field) :: Choose a field of the current
  entry to copy, including ones that are not displayed, such as the full
  commit id.  Candidates show a preview of the value.
- Key: ? w m (majutsu-row-copy-module) :: Copy the part of the row at point:
  the heading, the right-aligned tail, or the body.

Ordinary region copying copies the text you see, without the graph.

** Files, Diffs, and Operations
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: files-diffs-operations
:EXPORT_FILE_NAME: workflows/files-diffs-operations
:DESCRIPTION: Follow revisions into diffs, file snapshots, annotations, Ediff, process output, and operation history.
:END:
These commands start from a revision, usually the one at point in the log.

*** Diffing
**** Diff Transient
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: d (majutsu-diff) :: Open the Diff transient.
- Key: RET (majutsu-diff-dwim) :: On a revision, bookmark, or tag, show its
  diff without the transient.

#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Diff transient"
- Key: r :: Select revisions to diff (=--revisions=): several revisions, or
  a revset like =B::D=.
- Key: f / t :: Select the =--from= and =--to= revisions.
- Key: -- :: Limit the diff to [[#filesets][filesets]].  Completion offers
  the paths changed by the selected revisions; without a selection, by the
  revisions in the region, the revision at point, or =@=.  Opened from a
  log that is limited to filesets, the transient starts with the same limit, and
  so does ~RET~ on a revision there.
- Key: -g :: Toggle Git-style diff output.
- Key: -W :: Toggle color-words diff output.
- Key: -S :: Toggle stat output.
- Key: -s :: Toggle summary output.
- Key: -c :: Set context line count.
- Key: -b / -w :: Ignore whitespace amount / ignore all whitespace.
- Key: w :: Save the options as defaults; see
  [[#saved-defaults][Saved Defaults]].

**** Understanding =--revisions=
The =--revisions= argument accepts any revset that forms a /contiguous/ set of
commits. "Contiguous" means no gaps in the DAG, but *forks and merges are
allowed*.

Examples:
- =-r @= :: Changes in the working copy commit (default).
- =-r @-= :: Changes in the parent of the working copy.
- =-r B::D= :: Total changes from B through D.
- =-r 'A | B'= :: Valid only if A and B form a contiguous set; gaps produce an error.

When visiting a file from such a diff, Majutsu uses the exact range stored by
the diff buffer:
- On an *added* or *context* line: resolve the =--revisions= expression itself.
- On a *removed* line: resolve the parents of that expression
  (=REVSET-= in revset syntax).

Blob buffers require that the chosen side resolve to exactly one revision.
Majutsu reports an error rather than arbitrarily choosing one head or root.

*Note*: When the revset has multiple heads or roots, the target revision for
file visits may be ambiguous. For example, in an X-shaped history:
#+begin_example
  D   E       <- two heads
   \ /
    C
   / \
  A   B       <- two roots
#+end_example
If you diff =-r A::D | B::E=, there are two heads (D, E) and two roots (A, B).
The diff shows changes from the /merged/ parents to the /merged/ heads. If D
and E modify the same lines, the diff can show conflict markers. Inspection of
the combined diff still works, but visiting a blob from either ambiguous side
fails the single-revision check. Use =--from= / =--to= with single revisions
when precise file navigation matters.

**** Diff Buffer
The diff of one revision starts with that revision's metadata and its full
description, both collapsible.  A =--from= / =--to= comparison, or a revset
of several revisions, shows only the diff.

A stat summary is a collapsible directory tree: single-directory chains are
joined, and a rename appears under its destination with the source path in
the file's folded body.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Diff buffer" :mode majutsu-diff-mode
- Key: RET (majutsu-diff-visit-file) :: Visit the appropriate version of the
  file at point. For working copy diffs, added/context lines visit the workspace
  file while removed lines visit the parent-side blob. For committed changes, it
  visits the blob at the corresponding side.
- Key: C-j / C-<return> (Vanilla) (majutsu-diff-visit-workspace-file) :: Visit
  the workspace file, regardless of diff type.
- Key: C-<return> (Evil) (majutsu-diff-visit-workspace-file) :: Visit the
  workspace file without conflicting with Evil's ~C-j~ section navigation.
- Key: - (Vanilla) (majutsu-diff-less-context) :: Show fewer context lines
  around hunks; a prefix argument says how many fewer.
- Key: = (Evil) (majutsu-diff-less-context) :: Show fewer context lines
  around hunks; a prefix argument says how many fewer.
- Key: + (majutsu-diff-more-context) :: Show more context lines around hunks.
- Key: 0 (Vanilla) (majutsu-diff-default-context) :: Reset the context to the
  default.
- Key: ~ (Evil) (majutsu-diff-default-context) :: Reset the context to the
  default.
- Key: t (Vanilla) (majutsu-diff-toggle-refine-hunk) :: Toggle word-level refinement.
- Key: T (Vanilla) (majutsu-diff-toggle-fontify-hunk) :: Toggle syntax
  highlighting within diff hunks. With a prefix argument, cycle between
  highlighting the current hunk on selection and highlighting all hunks
  immediately.
- Key: j (Vanilla) (majutsu-jump-to-diffstat-or-diff) :: Jump from a file in
  the stat summary to its diff, and back.
- Key: g d (Evil) (majutsu-jump-to-diffstat-or-diff) :: Jump from a file in
  the stat summary to its diff, and back.
- Key: w (Vanilla) (majutsu-section-edit) :: Edit the description above the
  diff in place; see [[#editing-in-place][Editing Descriptions in Place]].
- Key: i (Evil) (majutsu-evil-section-edit) :: Edit the description above the
  diff in place.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
When Evil mode is active, Majutsu follows evil-collection's
conventions for Magit diff buffers: ~+~ still increases context, ~=~
decreases it, and =~= resets it to the default.

When =--color-words= is enabled, Majutsu renders the old/new line numbers in
the left margin and uses "..." lines to split hunks.
With refinement enabled, color-words hunks also show a shadow cursor on the
paired side (controlled by =smerge-refine-shadow-cursor=).
#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
With Vanilla bindings, file visits through ~RET~ or ~C-j~ still respect the
side at point by using stored line/column metadata from the color-words
backend.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
With Evil bindings, ~RET~ visits the side at point and ~C-<return>~ forces the
workspace file; ~C-j~ remains section navigation.  File visits use the same
stored line/column metadata from the color-words backend.

*** File and Blob Inspection
A blob buffer shows one file as of one revision.

- Command: majutsu-find-file :: Prompt for revset + path (defaulting from point
  when possible) and open that file as a blob.
- Command: majutsu-find-file-other-window :: Like ~majutsu-find-file~, but
  display the blob in another window.
- Command: majutsu-find-file-other-frame :: Like ~majutsu-find-file~, but
  display the blob in another frame.

Opening a file resolves its revset once and identifies the blob by workspace,
full commit ID, and path. Different versions of one change have separate
buffers. Revision actions, including Restore and Ediff, use the displayed
commit, not a newer version of the same change.

Explicit refresh resolves the original revset again. Missing files,
unsupported tree values, and warning-only reads leave the previous contents,
commit pin, and refresh target intact. Regular files and text file conflicts
are supported, including empty files; symlinks, submodules, and structural
conflicts are not blob-editing inputs.

Blob buffers are read-only snapshots with history-aware navigation:
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Blob buffer" :mode majutsu-blob-mode
- Key: p / n (majutsu-blob-previous / majutsu-blob-next) :: Jump to the previous
  or next revision that touched this file, while preserving cursor position as
  much as possible.
- Key: V (Vanilla) (majutsu-blob-visit-file) :: Jump to the workspace version of the same file.
- Key: C-c m (majutsu-blob-visit-magit) :: Open the current blob in Magit's blob viewer.
- Key: b (majutsu-annotate-addition) :: Start annotate for the current blob.
- Key: g (Vanilla) (revert-buffer) :: Revert or reload the current blob content.
- Key: g r (Evil) (revert-buffer) :: Revert or reload the current blob content.
- Key: e / C-x C-q (majutsu-blob-edit-start) :: Enter editable blob mode (wdired-style).

Blob navigation keys are disabled while editing, so blob-mode bindings do not
interfere with text edits.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Editable blob buffer" :mode majutsu-blob-edit-mode
- Key: C-c C-c (majutsu-blob-edit-finish) :: Apply changes through
  non-interactive =jj diffedit= and exit edit mode. Majutsu copies current
  buffer text into the diffedit right side and finishes automatically, without
  opening the right-side temp file buffer.
- Key: C-x C-q (majutsu-blob-edit-exit) :: Leave editable mode. If modified, it
  prompts to save or abort; if unchanged, it exits immediately.
- Key: C-c C-k (majutsu-blob-edit-abort) :: Abort blob edits, restore the
  original content, and restore the original cursor position.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
Evil normal-state behavior depends on whether the blob is read-only or
editable:

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Blob buffer" :mode majutsu-blob-mode :scope Evil :state Normal
- Key: i (majutsu-evil-blob-insert-dwim) :: Enter editable blob mode and stay in normal state.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Editable blob buffer" :mode majutsu-blob-edit-mode :scope Evil :state Normal
- Key: i (evil-insert-state) :: Enter insert state.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
Editable mode also changes cursor visuals (see
~majutsu-blob-edit-cursor-type~); with Evil, the normal-state cursor is updated
too.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
Evil bindings in blob buffers keep Evil's motions (~p~, ~n~, ~b~, ~e~, ~w~...)
untouched; blob commands live on the =g= prefix and =C-j= / =C-k=, mirroring
the annotate-mode keys:
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Blob buffer" :mode majutsu-blob-mode :scope Evil :state Normal
- Key: gj / C-j (majutsu-blob-next) :: Next revision touching the file.
- Key: gk / C-k (majutsu-blob-previous) :: Previous revision touching the file.
- Key: gb (majutsu-annotate-addition) :: Start annotate for the blob.
- Key: gf (majutsu-blob-visit-file) :: Visit the workspace version of the file.
- Key: gr :: Revert or reload the blob content.
- Key: q :: Bury the blob buffer.
- Key: RET (majutsu-diff-dwim) :: Show the diff of the blob's revision.

*** Annotate (Blame)
Annotate shows, for each line of a file, the revision that last changed it
(=jj file annotate=).  The navigation bindings below belong to
=majutsu-annotate-read-only-mode=, which is enabled by default through
=majutsu-annotate-read-only=.  Setting that option to nil keeps ordinary file
buffers editable with their editing bindings; revision blob buffers remain
read-only snapshots.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Annotate buffer" :mode majutsu-annotate-read-only-mode
- Key: b (Vanilla) (majutsu-annotate-addition) :: Enter annotate from a blob
  buffer. From an ordinary file buffer, use =M-x majutsu-annotate-addition=.
  When invoked again on an annotated chunk, jump to its parent revision (when
  available) and re-annotate there.
- Key: c (majutsu-annotate-cycle-style) :: Cycle heading/highlight/line styles
  (see =majutsu-annotate-styles=).
- Key: n / p (Vanilla) (majutsu-annotate-next-chunk / majutsu-annotate-previous-chunk) ::
  Move to the next or previous chunk.
- Key: C-j / g j / C-k / g k (Evil) (majutsu-annotate-next-chunk / majutsu-annotate-previous-chunk) ::
  Move to the next or previous chunk.
- Key: N / P (Vanilla) (majutsu-annotate-next-chunk-same-commit / majutsu-annotate-previous-chunk-same-commit) ::
  Move to the next or previous chunk from the same commit.
- Key: g J / g K (Evil) (majutsu-annotate-next-chunk-same-commit / majutsu-annotate-previous-chunk-same-commit) ::
  Move to the next or previous chunk from the same commit.
- Key: RET (Vanilla) (majutsu-annotate-show-commit) :: Show the chunk's revision diff.
- Key: M-w (majutsu-annotate-copy-hash) :: Copy the chunk change-id.
- Key: SPC (Vanilla) (majutsu-annotate-show-or-scroll-up) :: Scroll the diff
  window up if it is already open.
- Key: S-SPC (majutsu-annotate-show-or-scroll-down) :: Scroll the diff window
  down if it is already open.

*** Ediff and Diffedit
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer / dispatcher" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: E (majutsu-ediff) ::
  Open the Ediff transient.

Choose revisions with =--revisions= or =--from= / =--to=, as in the Diff
transient.  From a diff buffer, its range is the default.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Ediff transient"
- Key: e (majutsu-ediff-dwim) :: Compare the hunk, file, or revision at point
  in Ediff.
- Key: E (majutsu-ediff-edit) :: Edit one file of a revision with
  =jj diffedit=, using Ediff as the diff editor.  Majutsu asks for a changed
  file unless one is at point.  Edit the right-hand side and quit Ediff to
  hand the result back to jj.  With ~majutsu-diffedit-finish-on-save~,
  saving that file finishes the session.
- Key: m (majutsu-ediff-resolve) :: Resolve a conflicted file in a three-way
  Ediff session; see [[#conflict-resolution][Conflict Resolution]].  To be
  deprecated in Majutsu 0.8.
- Key: M (majutsu-ediff-resolve-with-conflict) :: Open a conflicted file with
  its conflict markers; see [[#conflict-resolution][Conflict Resolution]].

*** Operations and Evolution
jj records every change to the repository as an operation, and every
rewrite of a change as a new version of it.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: X (majutsu-op-transient) :: Open the Operations transient: log, diff,
  restore, revert, undo, and redo.
- Key: v (Vanilla) (majutsu-evolog) :: Open the evolution log of the revision
  at point.
- Key: ? v (Evil) (majutsu-evolog) :: Open the evolution log of the revision
  at point.  Evil keeps ~v~ for Visual state.

The operation log (~X l~) keeps jj's graph and compact format.  Its transient
takes =--limit=, =--reversed=, and =--no-graph=.  Browsing does not snapshot
the working copy.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Operation log" :mode majutsu-op-log-mode
- Key: d (majutsu-op-diff-transient) :: Open the operation diff transient for the
  operation at point.
- Key: u (majutsu-op-log-restore-at-point) :: Restore the repository to the
  operation at point, after confirmation.
- Key: r (majutsu-op-log-revert-at-point) :: Revert the operation at point,
  after confirmation.

An operation diff (~X d~) shows the two operations and the commits and
references that changed between them, for one operation or a =--from= /
=--to= range.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Operation diff" :mode majutsu-op-diff-mode
- Key: RET / v (majutsu-op-diff-evolog-at-point) :: Open the evolution log of
  the changed commit at point.

The evolution log shows the earlier versions of one change in jj's compact
format.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Evolution log" :mode majutsu-evolog-mode
- Key: RET (majutsu-evolog-diff-at-point) :: Show jj's inter-diff of the
  version at point against its predecessors.
- Key: l (Vanilla) (majutsu-evolog-transient) :: Open the evolution log
  options.

In the operation diff and the evolution log ~d~ remains the ordinary Diff
command.  In the operation log and the evolution log ~? w~ copies fields,
including full ids that are not displayed.

- Commands: majutsu-op-restore / majutsu-op-revert :: Restore the repository
  to an operation, or revert one operation, after confirmation.  Both are
  in the Operations transient.

* Manipulating
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: manipulating
:EXPORT_FILE_NAME: workflows/manipulating
:DESCRIPTION: Create, edit, rewrite, restore, and otherwise manipulate revision history.
:END:
** Creating Changes
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: o (majutsu-new) :: Open the New transient to specify options.

Direct log-buffer shortcuts:
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Log buffer" :mode majutsu-log-mode
- Key: O (majutsu-new-dwim) :: Create a new change on top of the revision at point (DWIM).
- Key: A (majutsu-new-with-after) :: Create a new change after the revision at point.
- Key: B (Vanilla) (majutsu-new-with-before) :: Create a new change before the revision at point.
- Key: I (Evil) (majutsu-new-with-before) :: Create a new change before the revision at point.

Where the new change goes, with the revision at point marked:
#+attr_demo: :kind choices
- On top (~O~) ::
  #+begin_example
  @  wqnwkozp (no description set)
  │ ○  xzyvoorv Add the renderer
  ├─╯
  ○  mxtrukyy Polish the index  ← at point
  ○  vzxpmxlw Import the parser core
  #+end_example
  The new change is a child of the revision at point.  Its other children
  stay where they are.
- After (~A~) ::
  #+begin_example
  ○  xzyvoorv Add the renderer  ← rebased
  @  wqnwkozp (no description set)
  ○  mxtrukyy Polish the index  ← at point
  ○  vzxpmxlw Import the parser core
  #+end_example
  The new change goes between the revision at point and its children, which
  are rebased onto it.
- Before (~B~, Evil ~I~) ::
  #+begin_example
  ○  xzyvoorv Add the renderer  ← rebased
  ○  mxtrukyy Polish the index  ← at point, rebased
  @  wqnwkozp (no description set)
  ○  vzxpmxlw Import the parser core
  #+end_example
  The new change goes between the revision at point and its parents.  The
  revision at point and its descendants are rebased onto it.

Useful transient entries include:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "New transient"
- Key: -r :: Parent revisions.
- Key: -A :: Insert after constraint.
- Key: -B :: Insert before constraint.
- Key: -m :: Set a message.
- Key: -e :: No edit (don't switch to the new change).
Runs: =jj new -r REV=

** Describing Changes
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: c (majutsu-describe) :: Edit the description of the revision at point
  in a description buffer.  Supports =--ignore-immutable= for immutable
  revisions.
Runs: =jj describe -r REV=

*** Description Buffer
jj waits while you edit the description in Emacs.  Finish to let jj use the
text, or cancel to make jj abort the command.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "JJ description buffer" :mode majutsu-jjdescription-mode
- Key: C-c C-c (with-editor-finish) :: Finish; jj uses the description.
- Key: C-c C-k (with-editor-cancel) :: Cancel; jj aborts the command.  The
  text is kept in the description history.
- Key: C-c C-d (majutsu-jjdescription-show-diff) :: Show the diff of the
  change being described.

Lines that start with ~JJ:~ are comments, and everything after
~JJ: ignore-rest~ is ignored.  Summary text beyond column 68 is highlighted
and the body fills at column 72; see
[[#customizing][Description Options]].

Majutsu remembers the descriptions of the session.  Recalling one replaces
the description and keeps jj's comments.  The history is not available when
several revisions are described in one buffer.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "JJ description buffer" :mode majutsu-jjdescription-mode
- Key: M-p (majutsu-jjdescription-prev-message) :: Recall the previous
  description.  A numeric prefix goes back that many.
- Key: M-n (majutsu-jjdescription-next-message) :: Recall the next
  description.
- Key: C-c M-p (majutsu-jjdescription-search-message-backward) :: Search
  backward through the history for a substring.
- Key: C-c M-n (majutsu-jjdescription-search-message-forward) :: Search
  forward through the history for a substring.
- Key: C-c M-s (majutsu-jjdescription-save-message) :: Save the current text
  to the history.

*** Editing Descriptions in Place
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: editing-in-place
:END:
Descriptions can also be edited where they are displayed: in the log, and
above the diff of one revision.  Like Wdired, a session makes every
description in the buffer editable while the rest stays read-only, so
several revisions can be reworded at once.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
#+attr_demo: :capture edit-in-place
- ~n n~ :: Move to a change.
- ~w~ :: Start editing.  Every description in the log is now a field.
- ~"Polish the "~ :: Type at the start of the description.
- ~C-n~ :: Move to the description below.
- ~" in Hiccup"~ :: Add to its end.
- ~C-c C-c~ :: Apply.  One =jj describe= rewords both changes.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
#+attr_demo: :capture edit-in-place-evil
- ~j j~ :: Move to a change.
- ~i~ :: Start editing.  Every description in the log is now a field.
- ~i~ :: Enter Insert state at the start of the description.
- ~"Polish the "~ :: Type.
- ~ESC j~ :: Back in Normal state, move down a line.
- ~0 w i~ :: Move to the description and enter Insert state.
- ~"Hiccup "~ :: Type.
- ~ESC Z Z~ :: Apply.  One =jj describe= rewords both changes.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Log and diff buffers" :mode majutsu-log-mode
- Key: w (Vanilla) (majutsu-section-edit) :: Start editing.
- Key: i (Evil) (majutsu-evil-section-edit) :: Start editing and stay in
  Normal state; a second ~i~ enters Insert state.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "In-place editing" :mode majutsu-section-edit-mode
- Key: C-c C-c (majutsu-section-edit-finish) :: Apply every changed
  description in one =jj describe=.
- Key: C-c C-k (majutsu-section-edit-abort) :: Discard the edits.
- Key: C-x C-q (majutsu-section-edit-exit) :: Leave; if anything changed, ask
  whether to apply it.
- Key: Z Z / Z Q (Evil) (majutsu-section-edit-finish / majutsu-section-edit-abort) ::
  Apply or discard.  ~:w~ applies too, and ~<escape>~ leaves like ~C-x C-q~.

The cursor changes while a session is active
(~majutsu-section-edit-cursor-type~).  Descriptions cut for alignment are
shown in full.

** Committing
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: C (majutsu-commit) :: Run =jj commit= through =with-editor=. This edits
  the working-copy description, finalizes that change, and lets jj create the
  next empty working-copy change on top.
Runs: =jj commit=

** Editing Changes
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: e (majutsu-edit) :: Move the working copy (@) to the revision
  at point.  From then on, changes to the files amend that revision and
  rewrite its descendants.  Supports =--ignore-immutable= for immutable
  revisions.
Runs: =jj edit REV=

** Abandoning
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Log buffer" :mode majutsu-log-mode
- Key: k (Vanilla) (majutsu-abandon) :: Remove the revision at point from visible
  history and rebase its descendants onto its parent(s). With an active region
  selection, Majutsu abandons all selected revisions. The operation remains
  recoverable through jj's operation history until that history is pruned.
- Key: x (Evil) (majutsu-abandon) :: Remove the revision at point from visible
  history and rebase its descendants onto its parent(s). With an active region
  selection, Majutsu abandons all selected revisions. The operation remains
  recoverable through jj's operation history until that history is pruned.
Runs: =jj abandon REV=

** Squashing
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: s (majutsu-squash) :: Open the Squash transient. You can select multiple
  source revisions (=--from=) to squash into a destination (=--into=).

Arguments:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Squash transient"
- Key: -f :: Source revisions (=--from=).
- Key: -t :: Destination revision (=--into=).
- Key: -i :: Open jj's configured diff editor for partial selection.
- Key: ~=t~ :: Choose jj's diff editor with =--tool=NAME=.
- Key: -o :: Onto destination.
- Key: -A / -B :: Insert after or before constraints.
- Key: -- :: Limit squash to [[#filesets][filesets]].
- Key: -k :: Keep commits that become empty after squashing.
- Key: -u :: Use the destination revision's description and discard source
  descriptions (=--use-destination-message=).
When opened from a log buffer, the source defaults to the selected revision(s)
at point or in the active region.  This default is retained when =-i= or
=--tool= starts jj's diff editor.

Runs: =jj squash --from SRC --into DEST [FILESETS...]=

** Splitting
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: S (majutsu-split) :: Open the Split transient. This allows you to split a
  revision into multiple parts.

Arguments:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Split transient"
- Key: -r :: Specify the revision to split.
- Key: -o :: Specify the destination (=--onto=).
- Key: -i :: Open jj's configured diff editor for partial selection.
- Key: ~=t~ :: Choose jj's diff editor with =--tool=NAME=.
- Key: -A / -B :: Insert after or before constraints.
- Key: -m :: Set a message for the first part.
- Key: -p :: Parallel split mode.
- Key: -- :: Limit split to [[#filesets][filesets]].
When opened from a log buffer, =-r= defaults to the revision at point before
the jj diff editor is started.

Runs: =jj split -r REV [FILESETS...]=

** Absorbing
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: a (majutsu-absorb) :: Open the Absorb transient.

Arguments:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Absorb transient"
- Key: -f :: Source revision (=--from=, default =@=).
- Key: -t :: Destination revset filters (=--into=, repeatable, default =mutable()=).
- Key: -i :: Open jj's configured diff editor for partial selection.
- Key: ~=t~ :: Choose jj's diff editor with =--tool=NAME= (implies interactive).
- Key: -- :: Limit absorb to [[#filesets][filesets]].
Runs: =jj absorb --from REV --into REVSETS... [FILESETS...]=

From a single-revision Diff buffer, use ~H~ to select a hunk, ~F~ for a file
or directory, and ~R~ for a region within a hunk; ~C~ clears these selections.
Press ~a~ or ~RET~ to absorb the selection using Majutsu's patch tool, without
enabling =-i=.  The selection can span files; opening the transient at a file
does not narrow it to that file.  Existing diff fileset limits still apply.

Only selected changes are considered for absorption.  jj assigns them to the
closest eligible ancestors, restricted by =--into=.  Unselected changes and
changes jj cannot assign remain in the source revision.  Explicit =-i= or
=--tool= requests instead use jj's diff editor, as described under
[[#interactive-patching][Interactive Patching]].

** Restoring
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: R (majutsu-restore) :: Open the Restore transient for undoing changes.

Arguments:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Restore transient"
- Key: -f :: Restore from a specific revision (=--from=).
- Key: -t :: Restore to a specific revision (=--to=).
- Key: -i :: Open jj's configured diff editor for partial selection.
- Key: ~=t~ :: Choose jj's diff editor with =--tool=NAME=.
- Key: -c :: Undo changes introduced by a revision (=--changes-in=).
- Key: -d :: Preserve descendant content while rebasing (=--restore-descendants=).
- Key: -- :: Limit restore to [[#filesets][filesets]].
When opened from a log buffer, =-c= defaults to the revision at point before
the jj diff editor is started.

Runs: =jj restore --from REV [FILESETS...]= or
=jj restore --changes-in REV [FILESETS...]=

** Rebasing
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: r (majutsu-rebase) :: Open the Rebase transient, in which you select
  sources and destinations in the log.

Arguments:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Rebase transient"
- Key: -s :: Rebase a revision and its descendants (=--source=).
- Key: -b :: Rebase a whole branch relative to the destination (=--branch=).
- Key: -r :: Rebase only the selected revisions while preserving dependencies
  among them (=--revision=).
- Key: -o :: Rebase onto destination parent(s) (=--onto=).
- Key: -A / -B :: Insert after or before the selected destination revisions.
- Key: -p :: Remove redundant parent edges while rebasing (=--simplify-parents=).
Exactly one source style (=-s=, =-b=, or =-r=) and one destination style
(=-o=, =-A=, or =-B=) may be active. The destination is required before
Majutsu executes the command.
Runs: =jj rebase --source SRC --onto DEST=

** Duplicating
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu dispatcher"
- Key: ? y (majutsu-duplicate) :: Open the Duplicate transient. Allows selecting
  source revisions and destination.

Arguments:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Duplicate transient"
- Key: -r :: Source revisions to duplicate.
- Key: -o :: Destination (=--onto=).
- Key: -A / -B :: Insert after or before constraints.
Runs: =jj duplicate -r REV=

** Reverting
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: V (Vanilla) (majutsu-revert) :: Open the Revert transient to apply
  reverse changes in one or more new revisions.
- Key: _ (Evil) (majutsu-revert) :: Open the Revert transient to apply reverse
  changes in one or more new revisions.

Arguments:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Revert transient"
- Key: -r :: Source revisions to revert (=--revision=, repeatable).
- Key: -o :: Apply reverse changes on top of revisions (=--onto=).
- Key: -A / -B :: Insert reverse changes after or before selected revisions.
Runs: =jj revert --revision REV --onto DEST=

** Metaediting
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu dispatcher"
- Key: ? m (majutsu-metaedit) :: Open the Metaedit transient. Revisions in the
  active region are selected initially, followed by the revision at point, then
  =@= as fallbacks.

Arguments:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Metaedit transient"
- Key: r / -r / c :: Toggle revisions at point or in the active region, read a
  revset, or clear the visual revision selections. Multiple revisions are
  supported.
- Key: -m / -a / -t :: Set message, author, and author timestamp.
- Key: -c / -u / -U / -f :: Toggle update-change-id, update-author,
  update-author-timestamp, or force-rewrite.
- Key: -I :: Ignore immutable revisions.
Runs: =jj metaedit [OPTIONS...] [REVSETS]...=

** Signing and Unsigning
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu dispatcher"
- Key: ? j (majutsu-sign) :: Open the Sign transient. Revisions in the active
  region are selected initially, followed by the revision at point, then =@= as
  fallbacks.
- Key: ? J (majutsu-unsign) :: Open the Unsign transient with the same visual revision selection.

Arguments:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Sign and Unsign transients"
- Key: r / -r / c :: Toggle revisions at point or in the active region, read a
  revset, or clear the visual revision selections.
- Key: -k :: Override the configured signing key for =jj sign=. Majutsu
  completes secret signing keys for the =gpg= and =gpgsm= backends, and the
  configured key plus =~/.ssh/*.pub= for the =ssh= backend. Arbitrary values
  remain available for backend-specific key formats. A commit-signing backend
  must be configured in jj.
- Key: -I :: Ignore immutable revisions.
Runs: =jj sign --revision REVSETS...= or =jj unsign --revision REVSETS...=

** Simplifying Parents
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu dispatcher"
- Key: ? P (majutsu-simplify-parents) :: Open the Simplify Parents transient.

Arguments:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Simplify Parents transient"
- Key: -s :: Simplify specified revision(s) together with descendant trees (=--source=).
- Key: -r :: Simplify specified revision(s) only (=--revision=).
- Key: -I :: Ignore immutable revisions.
If neither =--source= nor =--revision= is set, the Simplify action defaults to
selected region revisions, then the revision at point, then =@=.
Runs: =jj simplify-parents [--source REVSET] [--revision REVSET]=

** Arranging
~majutsu-arrange-tui~ runs jj's full-screen =arrange= command inside Emacs,
in a Ghostel terminal.  It is ~? A~ in the dispatcher; ~A~ in the log itself
is ~majutsu-new-with-after~.

Without a prefix argument it runs =jj arrange=, and jj's =revsets.arrange=
setting chooses the revisions.  With a prefix argument, Majutsu asks for a
revset.

Arrange needs a terminal, so Ghostel is required.  It works in local
repositories and over TRAMP to POSIX hosts.  When the TUI exits, the buffer
that started it is refreshed and the terminal transcript stays available.

** Undo and Redo
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: C-/ / C-? (Vanilla) (majutsu-undo / majutsu-redo) :: Undo or redo.
- Key: u / C-r (Evil) (majutsu-undo / majutsu-redo) :: Undo or redo.
Runs: =jj undo= or =jj redo=

** Sparse Working Copy
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: > (majutsu-sparse) :: Open the sparse working copy transient (set, add,
  remove, list, edit).

Actions:
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Sparse transient"
- Key: l (majutsu-sparse-list) :: List current sparse patterns in =*Majutsu Sparse*=.
- Key: s / S (majutsu-sparse-set / majutsu-sparse-set-clear) :: Set patterns by
  appending, or replace the entire set after clearing it first.
- Key: a / r (majutsu-sparse-add / majutsu-sparse-remove) :: Add or remove
  patterns incrementally.
- Key: e (majutsu-sparse-edit) :: Edit patterns via =jj sparse edit=.
- Key: R (majutsu-sparse-reset) :: Reset to all files (=jj sparse reset=).

Notes:
- Editing patterns opens a temporary =.jjsparse= buffer.
- Lines starting with ~JJ:~ are comments and are ignored by Jujutsu.
- Pattern completion includes current directories/files from =@=.
- Default "all files" state is represented by single pattern =.=.

** Interactive Patching
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: interactive-patching
:END:
Split, Squash, Absorb, and Restore can act on part of a change: selected
hunks, files, or lines.  You select in a diff buffer while the command's
transient is open.  The selection belongs to that transient and ends with
it; it is not a staging area.

*** Selecting
Open the diff of the revision (~RET~), then the transient of the command (~S~,
~s~, ~a~, or ~R~).  A Patch Selection group appears:

| Key | Command                             | Toggles                                            |
|-----+-------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------|
| ~H~ | ~majutsu-interactive-toggle-hunk~   | the hunk at point                                  |
| ~F~ | ~majutsu-interactive-toggle-file~   | a file, or everything below a stat-summary directory |
| ~R~ | ~majutsu-interactive-toggle-region~ | the lines in the region                            |
| ~C~ | ~majutsu-interactive-clear~         | clears the whole selection                         |

Selected hunks, lines, and files are highlighted, and the stat summary shows
which files are selected in full or in part.  On a directory, ~F~ selects
every file below it, folded ones included; on a fully selected directory it
clears them.

Run the command with its usual key or ~RET~.  Only the selection is acted
on:

| Command | Selected changes                                  | Everything else         |
|---------+---------------------------------------------------+-------------------------|
| Split   | go to the first commit                            | stays in the second     |
| Squash  | move to the destination                           | stays in the source     |
| Absorb  | are offered to jj, which assigns them to ancestors | stays in the source     |
| Restore | are undone                                        | is left alone           |

Absorb leaves selected changes that jj cannot assign in the source too;
=--into= limits the ancestors it considers.

A selection cannot be carried to another command; clear it first.

A change to the keystroke index also fixed the renderer.  To move the fix
into the parent, where the renderer was added, squash that one file:
#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
#+attr_demo: :capture select-file
- ~n~ :: Move to the change.
- ~RET~ :: Show its diff.
- ~s~ :: Open the Squash transient.  In a diff it offers Patch Selection.
- ~n n n n n~ :: Move to the file in the summary.
- ~F~ :: Select the file.
- ~RET~ :: Squash.  The diff shows what stayed.
- ~q~ :: Back in the log.
- ~n n~ :: Move to the parent.
- ~RET~ :: Its diff has the fix.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
#+attr_demo: :capture select-file-evil
- ~j~ :: Move to the change.
- ~RET~ :: Show its diff.
- ~s~ :: Open the Squash transient.  In a diff it offers Patch Selection.
- ~C-j C-j C-j C-j C-j~ :: Move to the file in the summary.
- ~F~ :: Select the file.
- ~RET~ :: Squash.  The diff shows what stayed.
- ~q~ :: Back in the log.
- ~j j~ :: Move to the parent.
- ~RET~ :: Its diff has the fix.

A change made two unrelated fixes.  To split the first off into a change of
its own, select its hunk:
#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
#+attr_demo: :capture select-hunk
- ~n~ :: Move to the change.
- ~RET~ :: Show its diff.
- ~S~ :: Open the Split transient.
- ~n n n n n n~ :: Move to the first hunk.
- ~H~ :: Select the hunk.
- ~RET~ :: Split.  jj asks for the descriptions of both parts.
- ~C-s "Trim" RET C-a C-k "Trim atoms"~ :: Describe the first part.
- ~C-s "Trim" RET C-a C-k "Split the input"~ :: Describe the second.
- ~C-c C-c~ :: Finish.  The diff shows the first part: the selected hunk.
- ~q~ :: Back in the log, the change has become two.
- ~n~ :: Move to the second.
- ~RET~ :: Its diff has the rest.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
#+attr_demo: :capture select-hunk-evil
- ~j~ :: Move to the change.
- ~RET~ :: Show its diff.
- ~S~ :: Open the Split transient.
- ~C-j C-j C-j C-j C-j C-j~ :: Move to the first hunk.
- ~H~ :: Select the hunk.
- ~RET~ :: Split.  jj asks for the descriptions of both parts.
- ~/ "Trim" RET c c "Trim atoms" ESC~ :: Describe the first part.
- ~n c c "Split the input" ESC~ :: Describe the second.
- ~C-c C-c~ :: Finish.  The diff shows the first part: the selected hunk.
- ~q~ :: Back in the log, the change has become two.
- ~j~ :: Move to the second.
- ~RET~ :: Its diff has the rest.

The working copy still has two lines of debugging among its changes.  To
discard just those lines, select them as a region:
#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
#+attr_demo: :capture select-region
- ~n~ :: Move to the working copy.
- ~RET~ :: Show its diff.
- ~R~ :: Open the Restore transient.
- ~n n n n n n~ :: Move to the hunk.
- ~C-n C-n C-n~ :: Move to the first line to discard.
- ~C-SPC C-n C-n~ :: Mark the two lines as a region.
- ~R~ :: Select the lines of the region.
- ~RET~ :: Restore.  The two lines are gone; the rest of the hunk stays.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
#+attr_demo: :capture select-region-evil
- ~j~ :: Move to the working copy.
- ~RET~ :: Show its diff.
- ~R~ :: Open the Restore transient.
- ~C-j C-j C-j C-j C-j C-j~ :: Move to the hunk.
- ~j j j~ :: Move to the first line to discard.
- ~V j~ :: Mark the two lines in Visual state.
- ~R~ :: Select the lines of the region.
- ~RET~ :: Restore.  The two lines are gone; the rest of the hunk stays.

*** Which Diffs Work
The diff must show what the command acts on:

- Split and Absorb need the diff of one revision.
- Squash needs the diff of one revision, which becomes the source.  Without
  a destination, Majutsu squashes into its parent.
- Restore takes the diff of one revision, as =--changes-in=, or a
  =--from= / =--to= comparison.

File limits of the diff still apply.  A selection whose diff has changed
since is rejected instead of being applied to other content.  Only one
patch operation, terminal editor, or blob save writes to a workspace at a
time; a second one is refused until the first ends.

*** jj's Diff Editors
=-i= and ~=t~ (=--tool=NAME=) choose in another way: they start jj's own
diff editor.  They take precedence over an Emacs selection, which is kept.
Note that =-t= is a destination option, not short for =--tool=.

jj's default editor, =:builtin=, is a terminal program.
~majutsu-diff-editor-host~ decides where editors run:

- =auto= :: The default: Ghostel when it is installed, otherwise an
  ordinary process.
- =ghostel= :: Always Ghostel.  Runs the built-in editor and other terminal
  tools.
- =process= :: For tools that open their own window; =:builtin= is refused.

Ghostel is optional and also works over TRAMP to POSIX hosts.  When Split
or Squash goes on to ask for a description, it opens in Emacs as usual;
locally this needs a working =emacsclient=.

*** Limits
- A deleted file is selected whole or not at all.
- Changes without text hunks, such as binary files and mode changes, are
  selected as whole files with ~F~, for Split, Squash, and Restore, in a
  Git-format diff.
- The mode change of a copied file cannot be kept without the copy.
- Hunks in new and renamed files are selected like any others.

*** Faces
- Face: majutsu-interactive-selected-hunk :: Selected hunks.
- Face: majutsu-interactive-selected-region :: Selected lines within a hunk.
- Face: majutsu-interactive-selected-file :: Whole-file changes and fully
  selected stat-summary entries.
- Face: majutsu-interactive-partially-selected-file :: Partially selected
  stat-summary files and directories.

* Conflict Resolution
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: conflict-resolution
:EXPORT_FILE_NAME: workflows/conflict-resolution
:DESCRIPTION: Detect Jujutsu conflicts, enter conflict mode, and choose or refine resolutions.
:END:
** Finding Conflicts
jj labels a conflicted revision =conflict= in the log.  The optional
[[#log-buffer][Conflicts section]] lists the working copy's conflicted files.

There are three ways to resolve a conflict:

| Way                     | Start with                    | Suits                                 |
|-------------------------+-------------------------------+---------------------------------------|
| Conflicts section       | ~M~                           | Seeing what collided; taking one text |
| Ediff                   | ~E m~                         | One file, at most two sides           |
| Conflict markers        | ~E M~, or open the file       | Editing the markers by hand           |

** Conflicts Section
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: conflicts-section
:END:
The diff of a conflicted revision has a Conflicts section between its
description and its changes.  It lists the conflicted files as a directory
tree, and each file's conflicts.

jj records a conflict as a sum of terms: a snapshot, and changes that each
lead from one text to another.  The section shows it that way.  Each term
goes by the label jj gave it: the revision it is from and, after a rebase,
a squash or a revert, what that revision was to the command.

- Most conflicts have three terms, and both changes start from the same
  one.  After a rebase that is the old parents of the rebased revision:
  one change leads =from= them =to= the destination, the other =to= the
  rebased revision.  Each shows what it did to the text they share.
- A conflict with more terms is shown in the order jj records them: the
  snapshot, then for each change a =from= term and a =to= term.  Its labels
  can contradict each other, since each still says what its revision was to
  the command that made it.  Such a conflict usually builds on an earlier
  one; resolve that first.

A =from= term keeps its text folded.  A term whose side has no such file
says so.

A revision inherits the conflicts of its parents.  The heading then names
the earlier change they come from; resolving them there settles the
descendants too.

#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer / dispatcher" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: M (majutsu-resolve) :: In a Conflicts section, resolve at point:
  on a term, the conflict becomes that text; on a conflict, choose among its
  terms and all sides one after the other; on a file, choose the side all of
  it becomes.  On the heading of conflicts that come from an earlier change,
  show that change at its conflicts.  Anywhere else, show the revision at
  point, or =@=, at its conflicts; with a prefix argument, choose a revision.

Each resolution is one jj operation and takes effect at once; ~C-/~ undoes
it.  The conflicts you have not resolved stay conflicts.

Taking a term drops what the other changes did.  Where both changes must
survive, ~RET~ (~majutsu-resolve-visit~) visits the file at the conflict or
term at point to edit it by hand: the working copy's file as it is, another
revision's as an editable blob.  Saving it refreshes the section.

A file that is not text has no conflicts to unfold, but a whole side of it
can be taken, as of a file one side lacks.  jj does that only for a conflict
with two sides.

The first of three changes was edited after the others were made on it.
The second edits the same two lines, so it is conflicted now, and the third
inherits that.  In one line the second change's text is the one to keep; the
other needs what both did:
#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
#+attr_demo: :capture resolve-conflict
- ~n~ :: Move to the working copy.  It and its parent are conflicted.
- ~M~ :: Show it at its conflicts.  They come from the parent.
- ~M~ :: On the heading, go there: the parent, at the same two conflicts.
- ~n n n n n~ :: Move to what the parent did to the first line.
- ~M~ :: Resolve with it.  One conflict is left.
- ~RET~ :: Visit the file at that conflict, to keep both changes.
- ~C-s "Goodbye, %s" RET "!"~ :: Give the parent's line what the other change added.
- ~C-c ^ RET~ :: Keep that line.
- ~C-c C-c~ :: Save it into the revision.
- ~q~ :: Back in the diff, the conflicts are gone.
- ~q~ :: Back in the log, neither change is conflicted.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
#+attr_demo: :capture resolve-conflict-evil
- ~j~ :: Move to the working copy.  It and its parent are conflicted.
- ~M~ :: Show it at its conflicts.  They come from the parent.
- ~M~ :: On the heading, go there: the parent, at the same two conflicts.
- ~C-j C-j C-j C-j C-j~ :: Move to what the parent did to the first line.
- ~M~ :: Resolve with it.  One conflict is left.
- ~RET~ :: Visit the file at that conflict, to keep both changes.
- ~/ "Goodbye, %s" RET f % l a "!" ESC~ :: Give the parent's line what the other change added.
- ~g r RET~ :: Keep that line.
- ~Z Z~ :: Save it into the revision.
- ~q~ :: Back in the diff, the conflicts are gone.
- ~q~ :: Back in the log, neither change is conflicted.

** Resolving with Ediff
~E m~ (~majutsu-ediff-resolve~) runs =jj resolve= with a three-way Ediff
session.  On a revision in the log it offers that revision's conflicted
files, otherwise the working copy's; candidates show the number of sides.

Quit Ediff to finish.  Majutsu then asks whether to save the merge;
answering no, or quitting without edits, leaves the conflict as it was.
Regions you left unresolved are written back with conflict markers, so jj
still reports them.

A conflict with more than two sides cannot be shown in Ediff; Majutsu opens
it with =jj diffedit= instead.

We plan to deprecate this command in Majutsu 0.8; the
[[#conflicts-section][Conflicts section]] handles any number of sides.

** Conflict Markers
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: conflict-markers
:END:
=majutsu-conflict-mode= is a minor mode for files that contain jj's conflict
markers.  It highlights the sides and has commands to keep one of them.

~E M~ (~majutsu-ediff-resolve-with-conflict~) opens a conflicted file with
the mode enabled, at the first conflict.  For a revision other than the
working copy, it opens an editable blob, and saving it resolves the conflict
in that revision.

- Command: majutsu-conflict-ensure-mode :: Enable the mode in a buffer with
  conflict markers.  A buffer with only Git-style markers (=|||||||= /
  ========) gets =smerge-mode= instead.

All of jj's marker styles are recognized, including long markers and
conflicts whose sides lack a final newline.

*** Commands
The keys that keep a term name it by number, as jj's own messages do.
=side #N= is the N-th term jj adds and =base #N= the N-th it subtracts, in
the order of the markers.  In the [[#conflicts-section][Conflicts section]]
a =from= term is a base, and the snapshot and the =to= terms are the sides.
The label after a marker says which revision a term is from.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
Emacs bindings use the prefix ~C-c ^~:
#+attr_keymap: :scope Vanilla
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Conflict buffer" :mode majutsu-conflict-mode :scope Vanilla :prefix "C-c ^"
- Key: n / p (majutsu-conflict-next / majutsu-conflict-prev) :: Jump to the
  next or previous conflict.
- Key: RET (majutsu-conflict-keep-current) :: Keep the term at point, side or
  base.
- Key: b (majutsu-conflict-keep-base) :: Keep base #1.  In a conflict with
  two sides that is the text both changes start from.
- Key: a (majutsu-conflict-keep-all) :: Concatenate every complete side
  snapshot in side order. Shared context is duplicated; conflicts with a
  nonempty base require confirmation.
- Key: s (majutsu-conflict-restyle) :: Re-render the conflict with different
  markers (diff -> snapshot, and snapshot <-> git for 2-sided conflicts). jj
  detects the marker style per conflict when parsing, so this only changes the
  presentation.
- Key: 1..9 (majutsu-conflict-keep-side) :: Keep side #N.
- Key: M-1..M-9 (majutsu-conflict-keep-side) :: Keep base #N.  A base does
  not belong to the side of the same number.
- Key: R (majutsu-conflict-refine) :: Refine conflict regions with word-level
  highlighting.

#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
Evil bindings are available in normal state:
#+attr_keymap: :scope Evil
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Conflict buffer" :mode majutsu-conflict-mode :scope Evil :state Normal
- Key: ]] / gj (majutsu-conflict-next) :: Jump to the next conflict.
- Key: [[ / gk (majutsu-conflict-prev) :: Jump to the previous conflict.
- Key: gb (majutsu-conflict-keep-base) :: Keep base #1.
- Key: gr RET (majutsu-conflict-keep-current) :: Keep the term at point.
- Key: gr a (majutsu-conflict-keep-all) :: Concatenate all complete side
  snapshots, confirming when the base is nonempty.
- Key: gr s (majutsu-conflict-restyle) :: Re-render with different markers.
- Key: gr 1..9 (majutsu-conflict-keep-side) :: Keep side #N.
- Key: gR 1..9 (majutsu-conflict-keep-side) :: Keep base #N.
- Key: ge (majutsu-conflict-refine) :: Refine the conflict.

*** Highlighting and Context Help
Conflict regions are highlighted like smerge-mode, generalized to
n-sided conflicts:
- Each side snapshot gets a distinct background face, cycling through
  ~majutsu-conflict-side-faces~ (=majutsu-conflict-side-1-face= inherits
  =smerge-upper=, =side-2= inherits =smerge-lower=).
- Base snapshots use =majutsu-conflict-base-face= (inherits =smerge-base=).
- Git-style (diff3) regions in mixed buffers (for example produced by
  ~majutsu-conflict-restyle~) are colored the same way. Buffers that contain
  only git-style conflicts are still handed to =smerge-mode= by
  ~majutsu-conflict-ensure-mode~; the two modes stay mutually exclusive.
- Eldoc describes the term at point: its label, then its number, as in
  =(side #2 of 3)=.
- =mouse-3= on a conflict pops up a resolution menu listing every side and
  base with its revision label. With =context-menu-mode= enabled, the entries
  join the standard context menu instead of replacing it.
- User Option: majutsu-conflict-auto-leave :: When non-nil (the default),
  resolving the last conflict in the buffer turns off
  =majutsu-conflict-mode=; undo re-enables it.

* Bookmarks
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: bookmarks
:EXPORT_FILE_NAME: repository/bookmarks
:DESCRIPTION: Create, move, track, and inspect Jujutsu bookmarks.
:END:
** Understanding Bookmarks
In Jujutsu, bookmarks are named references similar to Git branches. A local
bookmark normally targets one revision and may explicitly track a remote
bookmark; concurrent moves can also leave a bookmark with conflicted targets.

** Bookmark List
The bookmark list shows the local bookmarks, each with the state of its
remotes on its own line.

#+begin_example
main  ≡ origin            kzvx 1f2c first line of the description
topic ↑2 origin, ○ fork   qpwm 8a01 first line of the description
#+end_example

Unfold a bookmark for its remote bookmarks and, when its target is
conflicted, the targets jj removed (=-=) and added (=+=).  Git's special =@git= reference
appears under its bookmark only when it differs from the local target.
Bookmarks that exist on a remote only are in the [[#remote-list][remote list]].

- =≡= means the tracked reference is synchronized with the local bookmark.
- =○= means the reference is not tracked.
- =↑N= counts commits only in the local bookmark; =↓N= counts commits only
  in the remote reference.  Zero counts are omitted.  A lower bound is
  shown as =↑≥N= or =↓≥N= rather than an exact count.
- =×= means the local bookmark has been deleted while the tracked remote
  reference remains.  The deleted local bookmark stays visible.

Synchronized and untracked states use a muted color; local-only and
remote-only counts use distinct colors.  Hover over a row for the symbol
legend.  Folding is retained on refresh.

~RET~ on a bookmark shows the diff of its revision, and ~k~ (~x~ in Evil) deletes the
bookmark.  ~majutsu-bookmark-list~ moves to the local bookmark of the
bookmark at point, so from a remote bookmark in the remote list it leads to
its local row.  ~majutsu-bookmark-list-columns~ customizes the rows; it has
the format of the [[#log-columns][log columns]].

** Remote List
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: remote-list
:END:
~majutsu-git-remote-list~ shows the Git remotes with their fetch URL, a
distinct push URL, and how many of their bookmarks are tracked.

#+begin_example
origin  git@example.org:me/repo.git  2 tracked
fork  git@example.org:you/repo.git  1 tracked, 12 untracked
#+end_example

Unfold a remote for the bookmarks it holds, tracked or not, with the same
state symbols as the bookmark list.  This is where a bookmark that exists on
a remote only is found and tracked.  The bookmarks are rendered when the
remote is first unfolded.

On a remote, ~f~ fetches from it, ~r~ opens the Remotes transient, and ~k~ (~x~
in Evil) removes it.

The command moves to the remote at point: from a remote bookmark in the
bookmark list, it leads to the remote that holds it.

** Projects in the jjosh Build
jjosh configures remotes per scope: the repository itself or one registered
project.  Both lists therefore have one section per scope: =Repository=,
then each project under a heading with its name and directory.  The bookmark
list shows the scopes that have local bookmarks; the remote list shows every
project, and the repository when it has remotes of its own.

#+begin_example
parser  packages/parser  1 unsynced
  main  ≈ origin            kzvx 1f2c first line of the description
  topic ↑2 origin           qpwm 8a01 first line of the description
#+end_example

#+begin_example
parser  packages/parser
  origin  git@example.org:me/parser.git  2 tracked
vendor  third_party/vendor
  origin  https://example.org/vendor.git  filter :/src  37 untracked
#+end_example

Bookmarks appear under their project without the =#label= suffix; commands
still receive the full name.  Remotes act through their qualified name, such
as =origin#parser=.

In a repository of many projects, a tracked remote reference usually names
another commit than the local bookmark merely because unrelated history was
rewritten.  =≈= marks a project bookmark whose project directory is
identical on both sides; commit distances are shown only when the content
differs.  A push can still update the remote, because the history differs.
A project heading counts the bookmarks whose content differs as =N unsynced=.

~majutsu-git-fetch-project~ fetches the project at point from its default
remotes, and ~majutsu-project-at-point~ returns its name for your own
commands.  Neither has a default key binding.

** Bookmark Transient
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: b (majutsu-bookmark) ::
  Open the bookmark transient.

Actions:
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Bookmark transient"
- Key: l (majutsu-bookmark-list) :: List all bookmarks.
- Key: c (majutsu-bookmark-create) :: Create a new bookmark at point.
- Key: a (majutsu-bookmark-advance) :: Advance bookmarks using jj's configured
  default selection and target revset.
- Key: A (majutsu-bookmark-advance-to) :: Advance bookmarks using jj's default
  selection to an explicit target revset.
- Key: p (majutsu-bookmark-advance-patterns) :: Advance specific bookmark
  name(s)/pattern(s) using jj's configured default target revset.
- Key: s (majutsu-bookmark-set) :: Set or move an existing bookmark to the
  current revision.
- Key: m (majutsu-bookmark-move) :: Move a bookmark.
- Key: M (majutsu-bookmark-move-allow-backwards) :: Move bookmark(s) with
  =--allow-backwards=.
- Key: r (majutsu-bookmark-rename) :: Rename a bookmark.
- Key: d (majutsu-bookmark-delete) :: Delete a bookmark locally and record the
  deletion for propagation on a later push; this command does not contact a
  remote itself.
- Key: f (majutsu-bookmark-forget) :: Forget a bookmark without recording a
  deletion to push. A local name untracks corresponding remotes. In the
  jjosh build, an exact =NAME@REMOTE= forgets that remote bookmark until the
  next fetch, without forgetting the local bookmark. Git-tracking =NAME@git=
  is also supported in that build; its recreation depends on Git
  import/export and colocation.
- Key: t (majutsu-bookmark-track) :: Track a remote bookmark to create a local one.
- Key: u (majutsu-bookmark-untrack) :: Untrack a remote bookmark.

Forgetting a remote bookmark is a jjosh extension.  Only the jjosh build
offers remote bookmarks in Forget and defines ~majutsu-bookmark-forget-ref~.

* Tags
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: tags
:EXPORT_FILE_NAME: repository/tags
:DESCRIPTION: Create, move, delete, and inspect Jujutsu tags.
:END:
** Understanding Tags
In Jujutsu, tags are lightweight refs that point to revisions, similar to Git
tags. Majutsu wraps =jj tag set/list/delete= and follows jj semantics where
creating and moving tags both use =tag set= (moving requires =--allow-move=).

** Tag Transient
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu dispatcher"
- Key: ? t (majutsu-tag) :: Open the tag transient.

Actions:
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Tag transient"
- Key: l (majutsu-tag-list) :: List tags in a dedicated buffer.
- Key: s (majutsu-tag-set) :: Set tag(s). Uses completion and allows new names.
- Key: m (majutsu-tag-move) :: Move existing tag(s) to another revision (internally =--allow-move=).
- Key: d (majutsu-tag-delete) :: Delete tag(s) by name or pattern.

Prompts complete existing tags; Set also accepts new names, and Set and
Delete accept patterns.

In the tag list, ~RET~ on a tag shows the diff of its revision and ~k~
(~x~ in Evil) deletes the tag.

* Git Integration
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: git-integration
:EXPORT_FILE_NAME: repository/git-integration
:DESCRIPTION: Synchronize Git remotes and upload changes for Gerrit review.
:END:
** Git Transient
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Majutsu buffer / dispatcher" :mode majutsu-mode
- Key: G (Vanilla) (majutsu-git-transient) ::
  Open the Git transient: push, fetch, remotes, clone, and Gerrit upload.
- Key: ? G (Evil) (majutsu-git-transient) ::
  Open the Git transient: push, fetch, remotes, clone, and Gerrit upload.

** Pushing
#+attr_reference: :kind command-binding :interface "Git transient"
- Key: p (majutsu-git-push-transient) :: Open the Push transient. You can push
  bookmarks, tags, revisions, or changes.

Arguments:
#+attr_reference: :kind transient-argument :interface "Push transient"
- Key: -a :: Push all bookmarks and tags.
